sources.title: Thomas Risley Odhiambo (Q3525519) -- verified live via Wikidata (2026-10-30): English label 'Thomas Risley Odhiambo', description 'Kenyan entomologist (1931-2003)', born 1931-02-04, died 2003-05-26, citizenship Kenya, no Korean label, no P18 image. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

American Academy of Arts and Sciences Archives, finding aid for the records of the International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (ICIPE), 1968-1985 (historical note read in full). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: it records that Carl Djerassi proposed a model for advanced research centres in developing countries in 1967, that Odhiambo of University College, Nairobi read it and wrote proposing an insect physiology and endocrinology institute for East Africa, that an interim organizing group met in 1968-1970 led on the American side by the Academy and the National Academy of Sciences, that ICIPE was established in Nairobi in 1970, that Odhiambo was its first Director, and who funded it. Neutral archival description of the founding and of shared credit.

ICIPE (International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology), 'Our History', read in full: his Cambridge PhD under Vincent Wigglesworth, the 1967 Science review calling for centres of excellence, the support of Carl Djerassi, the 21 sponsoring national academies, the opening in 1970 in rented barracks, and his remark about getting the best people first. Institutional text from the organisation he founded, so admiring.

Rachel Galun, 'Thomas Risley Odhiambo (1931-2003): an appreciation' (International Journal of Tropical Insect Science 24(2), 2004, pp. 122-124), read in full from the publisher PDF: locust and tsetse research, his early taxonomic work on plant bugs, the 1967 Science plea, the part-time external directors model, 21 sponsoring academies, the tension between basic-science sponsors and applied-research donors at ICIPE, the ARPPIS postgraduate programme, the African Academy of Sciences and two journals. Obituary by a long-time colleague (Hebrew University), so admiring; it notes that ICIPE later narrowed its pest focus at the advice of collaborators and donors.

Annalee N. Mengech and Ahmed Hassanali, 'Thomas Risley Odhiambo: Founding Editor of Insect Science and Its Application' (Insect Science and its Application 23(3), 2003, pp. 159-161), read in full from the publisher PDF: his Makerere and Cambridge training, the 1967 Science article (vol. 156 as cited there), the first-year budget of US$10,000 and his own account of funding difficulty, ARPPIS from 1983, the East African Academy, the Kenya National Academy of Sciences, the African Academy of Sciences and ICIPE Science Press, his reluctant departure as ICIPE Director in 1994 and the later RANDFORUM. Obituary by two journal editors from the institute, so admiring; dates differ from other sources and are not used where they conflict.

Carl Djerassi, 'Can science work in Africa?' (Web of Stories video interview, transcript read in full): Djerassi's own account that the Kenyan scientist Tom Odhiambo read his Pugwash article and wrote asking about trying the model in Kenya, and that they 'came together' to found ICIPE. First-person recollection by the collaborator, independent of the institute, supporting shared credit for the founding.

James Njoroge, 'Kenya mourns death of a scientific giant: Thomas Odhiambo' (SciDev.Net, 28 May 2003), read in full: founding director of ICIPE, role in the African Academy of Sciences, vice presidency of the Third World Academy of Sciences, RANDFORUM, the 1987 Africa Prize for Leadership, and a tribute from a former Kenya National Academy of Sciences president. Independent news report of the death, but it relays tributes.

Kenya National Academy of Sciences, member profile of Prof. Odhiambo (Founding Fellow, 1986), read in full: education, University of Nairobi teaching, founder and Director of ICIPE, fellowships and academy roles, some 110 publications mainly on hormonal control of insect reproduction, early authority on plant bug taxonomy. Academy profile of a founding member; says ICIPE director since 1970 and that he joined Nairobi in 1965.

Building Endogenous Capacity for the Management of Neglected Tropical Diseases in Africa: The Pioneering Role of ICIPE (PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases, 2014), read for the Odhiambo section: the genesis of ICIPE in his November 1967 Science paper, his succession as director-general in 1994 by Hans Herren, and the naming of the Mbita campus after him. Scholarly article by ICIPE-affiliated authors, so partly institutional.

Rachel Galun and Onesmo K. ole-MoiYoi, 'Thomas Risley Odhiambo (1931-2003)' (Nature 425, 142, 11 September 2003): only the opening preview paragraphs were readable (paywalled); used only for his 1965 sole-authored Nature paper, his Makerere studies and Kericho and Uganda posts, and the Miridae discoveries.

proactive_agency.rationale: [src_odhiambo_amacad_icipe, src_odhiambo_djerassi_wos, src_odhiambo_galun_2004 | 1967-1970 | archive + collaborator interview + colleague obituary] Asked by Science to review African science, he wrote a plea for centres of excellence, then on reading Djerassi's proposal wrote to him suggesting an insect physiology institute in East Africa (the Academy archive and Djerassi agree), and went on to be ICIPE's first Director. The initiative is stated by an archive and by the partner, not only by his own institute; credit for the model is shared with Djerassi.

impact_motivation.rationale: [src_odhiambo_mengech_2003, src_odhiambo_galun_2004, src_odhiambo_icipe_history | 1967-1994 | obituaries + institution] His 1967 article argued science should raise smallholder livelihoods and tackle crop and vector problems; he built ARPPIS (1983) to train African postgraduates, founded ICIPE Science Press and a journal, and co-founded academies, documented by two obituaries and ICIPE's history. The stated purpose comes from admiring sources close to him, so confidence stays moderate.

leadership_drive.rationale: [src_odhiambo_amacad_icipe, src_odhiambo_mengech_2003, src_odhiambo_knas, src_odhiambo_scidev_2003 | 1970-1995 | archive + obituary + academy profile + news] He was the first Director of ICIPE (archive), founder-chairman of the Kenya National Academy of Sciences and founder president of the African Academy of Sciences (obituary, academy profile, news); start and end years of these posts differ between sources and are not scored. His 1994 departure from ICIPE is described as reluctant (Mengech and Hassanali); the reasons are not documented in any source read and are not scored.

persuasiveness.rationale: [src_odhiambo_mengech_2003, src_odhiambo_galun_2004, src_odhiambo_icipe_history | 1967-1986 | obituaries + institution] The 1967 article drew more than 1000 requests for reprints and 21 national academies came to sponsor ICIPE; he said he held eleven international meetings to win people over to non-insecticide control; Galun credits his diplomacy with balancing basic-science sponsors and applied-research donors. All admiring. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): lowered from 68 / 0.52 to 64 / 0.48 because the reprint count and the persuasion claims rest on admiring obituaries and his own interview quote, not on independent evidence.

collaboration.rationale: [src_odhiambo_amacad_icipe, src_odhiambo_djerassi_wos, src_odhiambo_galun_2004, src_odhiambo_mengech_2003 | 1968-1986 | archive + collaborator interview + obituaries] ICIPE was set up with Djerassi and a joint American academy committee, with part-time research directors from sponsoring academies, and ARPPIS ran with 27 African universities (Mengech and Hassanali). The multi-party design is documented, but his personal working relationships are not described in detail, so the row stays modest.

persistence.rationale: [src_odhiambo_mengech_2003, src_odhiambo_icipe_history | 1970-1994 | obituary + institution] The first-year budget was US$10,000, the first headquarters were rented wooden barracks and a garage, and he told an interviewer that research gets low priority because people believe technology can be bought; he led ICIPE for about two decades afterwards (Mengech and Hassanali; ICIPE history). Years of leadership are given inconsistently by sources, so no length is stated.

mastery_orientation.rationale: [src_odhiambo_galun_2004, src_odhiambo_knas, src_odhiambo_nature_obit, src_odhiambo_icipe_history | 1953-1966 | obituaries + academy profile] He built a record in plant bug taxonomy (over 20 papers describing new genera and dozens of species, per Galun), then a Cambridge PhD on locust reproductive physiology under Vincent Wigglesworth with a series of papers, whom Galun says considered him his best student (a retrospective claim by an admiring colleague). Records of deep specialist work in two fields; no independent assessment of the science was read.

portrait.reason: No rights-clear portrait was found. Wikidata has no image (P18), a Commons search for the name returned no photograph of him, and the only photographs located (the Queens' College alumni page, ICIPE and academy pages, news sites) carry no stated licence, creator or date. Not guessed. Next step: obtain a documented photograph with a stated licence or a written permission from ICIPE, the African Academy of Sciences, the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene archive or a news agency, or find a dated pre-1931 image (none exists for a man born in 1931).

ZERO POLITICS: the president's condolence message, the Africa Prize for Leadership (shared with a head of state), the RANDFORUM effort to rally political commitment and the 'Group of 7' presidents are not scored; the 1994 departure from ICIPE is recorded as reluctant per one obituary and its cause is not scored. KOREAN NAME: no Wikidata Korean label; 토머스 오디암보 is a transliteration chosen by the agent (not an established Korean name). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: American Academy of Arts and Sciences Archives, ICIPE records finding aid (https://www.amacad.org/archives/fa/icipe), with the ICIPE history page. READ (8 substantive): AmAcad archive note, ICIPE history, Galun 2004, Mengech and Hassanali 2003, Djerassi interview transcript, SciDev.Net obituary, KNAS profile, PLoS NTD 2014 article (Odhiambo section); the Nature obituary was read only as a preview. PERSPECTIVES: neutral archive, founder's institute, colleague obituaries, the collaborator Djerassi, a news report, a national academy. COUNTER-VOICES: thin: no critical or adversarial source was located; Galun reports the basic-versus-applied funding tension, Mengech and Hassanali the reluctant 1994 departure. A search surfaced a personal blog (Arnold van Huis) and a Guardian obituary claiming he was removed in 1994 after conflicts with ICIPE's governing body over use of donor funds; neither could be opened, so that claim is NOT used and is flagged for the lead; the unexplained 1994 departure caps the leadership and persistence rows. SHARED CREDIT: ICIPE's design rests on Djerassi's 1967 model and an American academy committee; Odhiambo is credited with the Science article, the proposal to Djerassi, the East African base and being first Director; the card text says so. DATE CONFLICTS (not resolved, not used): ICIPE founding 1967/1969/1970 (archive says established 1970); AAS founding 1983 vs 1985/1986/1987 and his presidency end 1995/1998/1999; Mombasa vs Alego birthplace; Odhiambo's own 1987 Scientist profile page was paywalled. NOT OPENED: Science 1967 article, Royal Society memoir (none located; he does not appear to have a Royal Society memoir), The Scientist 1987, Odhiambo's own books, Britannica. SELF-CALIBRATION: rows reviewed: persuasiveness, impact_motivation, proactive_agency. Lowered: persuasiveness 68/0.52 -> 64/0.48 (admiring obituaries and his own interview quote only). impact_motivation kept (two obituaries plus ICIPE history and documented programmes); proactive_agency kept (archive and Djerassi agree).
